facts.claim: ObjectCaptureSession exists on iOS 17.0+ (iPadOS 17.0+), NOT macOS. It is a @MainActor class, conforms to Identifiable, Observable, Sendable. Session state machine drives image capture; reconstruction is a separate PhotogrammetrySession phase.
facts.notes: isSupported: 'If false, attempting to create an ObjectCaptureSession will result in a runtime error.' Requires LiDAR + A14 or later, back camera only, no Simulator (Apple forum 731148 / 734086, sample README). iPhone 13 Pro Max (A15 + LiDAR) qualifies. Conformance to Identifiable means `.id(session.id)` works in SwiftUI (sample uses it).

facts.claim: Start the session exactly once with an EMPTY writable images directory and an optional empty checkpoint directory; non-empty directory or unwritable location moves the session to .failed.
facts.notes: 'This call is only valid once on a newly created session.' Errors: ObjectCaptureSession.Error.directoryNotEmpty(URL), .insufficientStorage(requiredBytes: Int64), .sensorFailed, .trackingFailed, .cancelled. checkpointDirectory 'also needs to point to an empty, writable directory'. isOverCaptureEnabled lets the session keep shooting past maximumNumberOfInputImages (extras stored in Images/ but skipped by on-device reconstruction, meant for Mac processing). Apple sample sets isOverCaptureEnabled = true and checkpointDirectory = <capture>/Checkpoint/.

facts.claim: Capture state machine cases and transitions: initializing -> ready -> (detecting) -> capturing -> finishing -> completed, or failed(any Error) at any time. CaptureState is Equatable; failed compares equal to any failed regardless of payload.
facts.notes: 'A session is over when the capture state is set to .completed or .failed.' Observe with `for await newState in session.stateUpdates`. ObjectCaptureSession.Updates<Element> where Element: Sendable is an AsyncSequence. cancel() ends in .failed(ObjectCaptureSession.Error.cancelled) which the sample treats as a normal restart.

facts.claim: Control methods: startDetecting() (object mode: ready -> detecting, returns false if not in .ready or no horizontal plane at screen center), resetDetection() (detecting -> ready), startCapturing() (detecting -> capturing in object mode, or ready -> capturing directly for area/freeform mode), finish() (capturing -> finishing -> completed; ignored in any other state), cancel(), pause()/resume().
facts.notes: Area mode (WWDC24): 'Simply skip the call to startDetecting and proceed directly to startCapturing.' There is no CaptureMode enum in the API; the sample app models captureMode (.object/.area) itself. pause(): 'Call this when object capture view is not visible, such as when a help screen is shown.' If the ObjectCaptureView is removed from the hierarchy the session pauses automatically; when it is only blurred under a sheet you must call pause()/resume() yourself (sample comment).

facts.claim: Multi-pass flows: beginNewScanPassAfterFlip() (object flipped; session goes back to .detecting/ready for a new bounding box, images go to the same folder and PhotogrammetrySession stitches them) and beginNewScanPass() (same box, new orbit at a different height; stays in .capturing). userCompletedScanPass becomes true when the capture dial is full and resets on either call. Both are only valid in object-centric scanning (not area mode).
facts.notes: Apple recommends 3 scan passes (3 orientations if flippable, else 3 heights). 'beginNewScanPassAfterFlip() should be called AFTER the object flipped for best results.' beginNewScanPass 'will throw if the session is not in .capturing state' (doc wording; signature is not marked throws). Sample: after each completed pass it calls `session.beginNewScanPass()` when !isObjectFlippable else `session.beginNewScanPassAfterFlip()`. Feedback .objectNotFlippable says the object is too textureless to stitch after a flip.

facts.claim: Manual and automatic shots: requestImageCapture() only works in .capturing when canRequestImageCapture is true; isAutoCaptureEnabled (iOS 18) can disable auto-capture so only manual shots are taken. numberOfShotsTaken counts both; maximumNumberOfInputImages is the device-specific on-device reconstruction limit and the session stops capturing at that limit unless isOverCaptureEnabled.
facts.notes: The concrete value of maximumNumberOfInputImages on an iPhone 13 Pro Max is not documented; read it at runtime (sample shows '%d/%d' shots/max in the UI). Community evidence (Apple forum 738944, non-Apple poster) says 'image limit of 1000 images' on iOS; WWDC24 says Macs handle up to 2000. Treat the number as unknown until logged on device. Sample enforces its own minimum of 10 images before allowing reconstruction.

facts.claim: Feedback set and tracking state: feedback is a Set<Feedback> with 9 cases; cameraTracking reports ARKit tracking and the ARKit coaching overlay appears automatically when tracking is not .normal (hide your own overlay then).
facts.notes: objectNotDetected: detection failed and a default manual box is shown. overCapturing: shots beyond maximumNumberOfInputImages will not be used on device. environmentTooDark stops auto-capture. Sample shows its overlay only when `session.cameraTracking == .normal && !session.isPaused`.

facts.claim: ObjectCaptureView is a SwiftUI view (generic over an Overlay view) that renders the whole Apple capture UI (camera feed, reticle, bounding box handles, capture dial, coaching overlay). You must host the session in it; an overlay closure and normal ZStack siblings let you add your own controls. hideObjectReticle(_:) (iOS 18) hides the reticle in .ready state for area mode. Removing the view pauses the session; re-creating a view from the same session resumes it.
facts.notes: Sample: `ObjectCaptureView(session: session, cameraFeedOverlay: { GradientBackground() }).hideObjectReticle(appModel.captureMode == .area).blur(...).transition(.opacity)` with `CaptureOverlayView(session:)` as a ZStack sibling, `.id(session.id)`. The bounding box UI, capture dial, and reticle cannot be restyled; only overlaid. Note `init(session:)` alone requires Overlay to be inferable; use `ObjectCaptureView(session: s)` (works via the plain initializer) or the overlay form.

facts.claim: ObjectCapturePointCloudView renders the current pass's LiDAR/feature point cloud with a turntable gesture for review before finish(); showShotLocations(_:) (iOS 18) draws camera shot positions. Presenting it pauses capture.
facts.notes: WWDC23: 'This will pause the capture session and let you interact with the point cloud to preview it from all angles.' Sample shows it inside the onboarding sheet between passes.

facts.claim: PhotogrammetrySession runs on iOS 17.0+ (also macOS 12+). Two initializers: from an images directory URL or from any Sequence of PhotogrammetrySample (iterated lazily once). Check isSupported first.
facts.notes: 'On the first process() call the data in the input source will be ingested entirely and inputComplete produced ... before any request processing progress will begin.' Throws if isProcessing is still true for a previous batch. cancel() is asynchronous: wait for .processingCancelled before creating a new session. Errors: PhotogrammetrySession.Error.insufficientStorage(requiredBytes: Int64), .invalidImages(URL), .invalidOutput(URL) plus internal `.processError` seen in the wild (forum 794169) with localizedDescription carrying cv3dapi codes.

facts.claim: On iOS only Detail.reduced is available. The cases .preview, .medium, .full, .raw are macOS/Mac Catalyst only and .custom is macOS 14 / Catalyst 17 only, so referencing them in iOS code is a compile-time availability error, not just a runtime limit. reduced = <50k triangles, ~10 MB, 2048x2048 diffuse + normal + ambient occlusion maps.
facts.api: enum PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Detail { case reduced /* iOS 17+, macOS 12+ */; case preview, medium, full, raw /* macOS 12+/Catalyst 15+ only */; case custom /* macOS 14+/Catalyst 17+ only */ }
facts.availability: .reduced iOS 17.0+; all other cases macOS only
facts.notes: Doc text: 'On iOS, only one detail level, .reduced, is currently supported. This level is optimized for generation and viewing entirely on mobile devices.' Per-case JSON platforms lists confirm iOS is absent for the other cases. Configuration.customDetailSpecification, .meshPrimitive (macOS 15) and MeshPrimitive enum are likewise not iOS. Texture table: reduced 2048x2048 (42.7 MB uncompressed at runtime), medium 4096, full 8192.

facts.claim: Request cases: modelFile(url:detail:geometry:) writes a USDZ (or, per docs, an OBJ folder when url is a directory), modelEntity(detail:geometry:) returns an in-memory ModelEntity, bounds returns a BoundingBox the size of the model, pointCloud returns sparse points, poses returns camera poses early in processing. Detail and geometry default to .reduced / nil so `.modelFile(url: out)` compiles on iOS.
facts.notes: Apple's iOS sample only handles .modelFile and comments '.modelEntity, .bounds, .poses, .pointCloud: Not supported yet' in its switch (it does not request them; unclear if they work on iOS). Sample output path: `<capture>/Models/model-mobile.usdz`. Geometry lets you crop/transform the output with a bounding box.

facts.claim: OBJ output from PhotogrammetrySession on iOS is documented ('saved to a USDZ file or a folder (for OBJ output)') with iOS 17 availability, but the only field report is community: passing a directory URL created with `appendingPathComponent("Models/", isDirectory: true)` produced OBJ output; a non-directory URL without .usdz fails with 'Output URL must be specify a .usdz extension file!'. Not confirmed by Apple on iOS specifically.
facts.api: case modelFile(url: URL, detail: PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Detail = .reduced, geometry: PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Geometry? = nil)
facts.availability: iOS 17.0+ (doc); OBJ-on-iOS confirmed only by forum users
facts.notes: If OBJ export must be guaranteed, fall back to loading the USDZ with ModelIO (MDLAsset(url:)) and `MDLAsset.export(to:)` which supports .obj and .stl on iOS 9+ (`class func canExportFileExtension(_:) -> Bool`, `func export(to URL: URL) throws`). Textures/materials survive to .mtl only partially via ModelIO; verify on device.

facts.claim: Configuration for iOS: isObjectMaskingEnabled (default true; auto-generates masks if samples have none; set false for area/scene captures), sampleOrdering (.unordered/.sequential), featureSensitivity (.normal/.high), checkpointDirectory (iOS: reuse the ObjectCaptureSession checkpoint folder or an interrupted session's folder to resume/speed up; must be unique per images folder), ignoreBoundingBox (iOS 18: ignore embedded box and return all geometry; combine with isObjectMaskingEnabled = false to keep the whole scene).
facts.notes: Apple sample: `var configuration = PhotogrammetrySession.Configuration(); if captureMode == .area { configuration.isObjectMaskingEnabled = false }; configuration.checkpointDirectory = captureFolderManager.checkpointFolder; photogrammetrySession = try PhotogrammetrySession(input: captureFolderManager.imagesFolder, configuration: configuration)`. ignoreBoundingBox is the hook for Mapper's 'capture a whole scene' use; the doc warns the mesh 'will likely need post-processing'. checkpointDirectory doc says reconstruction can resume from an earlier interrupted PhotogrammetrySession on iOS.

facts.claim: Outputs is an AsyncSequence of PhotogrammetrySession.Output; iterate with `for try await output in session.outputs` (or `for await` after wrapping). Cases: inputComplete, requestProgress(_:fractionComplete:), requestProgressInfo(_:_:) with estimatedRemainingTime and processingStage, requestComplete(_:_:), requestError(_:_:), processingComplete, processingCancelled, invalidSample(id:reason:), skippedSample(id:), automaticDownsampling, stitchingIncomplete.
facts.notes: The outputs sequence is infinite; Apple's sample wraps it in `UntilProcessingCompleteFilter` that ends after .processingComplete or .processingCancelled. Always include `@unknown default`. automaticDownsampling means the session shrank images for memory. stitchingIncomplete indicates a flipped side did not stitch (non-rigid or shiny object).

facts.claim: PhotogrammetrySample carries one image plus metadata; on iOS 18 `init(contentsOf:)` loads a HEIC written by ObjectCaptureSession and populates depthDataMap, depthConfidenceMap, gravity, camera (transform/intrinsics), boundingBox (unit-cube transform, iOS 18), sessionID and scanPassID. objectMask must be kCVPixelFormatType_OneComponent8 at image size; id must be in [0, 2147483647].
facts.api:
struct PhotogrammetrySample {
  init(id: Int, image: CVPixelBuffer)
  init(contentsOf url: URL) async throws            // iOS 18.0+
  let id: Int
  let image: CVPixelBuffer
  var metadata: [String : Any]
  var depthDataMap: CVPixelBuffer?
  var depthConfidenceMap: CVPixelBuffer?
  var gravity: CMAcceleration?
  var objectMask: CVPixelBuffer?
  var orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation
  var captureTime: Date?
  var camera: PhotogrammetrySample.Camera?
  var boundingBox: simd_float4x4? { get }             // iOS 18.0+
  var scanPassID: Int?
  var sessionID: UUID?
}
facts.notes: Field data (forum 794169): ObjectCaptureSession HEICs are 3024x4032 with an embedded 192x256 8-bit depth channel plus CameraCalibrationData, PointCloudData, TemporalDepthPointClouds metadata. Depth lets photogrammetry recover true metric scale ('If your source images contain depth data, RealityKit uses it to calculate the real-world size'). boundingBox 'can be factored as an SRT ... using Transform(matrix:)' giving the user-chosen box dimensions without reconstruction.

facts.claim: Apple's official sample (Scanning objects using Object Capture, WWDC23 10191 + WWDC24 10107, Xcode 16 version) targets iOS 18.0, uses @Observable AppDataModel + CaptureFolderManager creating Documents/<ISO8601 timestamp>/{Images/, Checkpoint/, Models/}; images are HEIC named IMG_xxxx.HEIC; final USDZ written to Models/model-mobile.usdz; Info.plist only needs NSCameraUsageDescription. No special entitlements, so it works with a free Apple ID sideload.
facts.api: CaptureFolderManager: captureFolder = URL.documentsDirectory/<timestamp>/ ; imagesFolder = .../Images/ ; checkpointFolder = .../Checkpoint/ ; modelsFolder = .../Models/
facts.availability: Sample: iOS 18.0+, Xcode 16; underlying APIs iOS 17+
facts.notes: Downloaded and read the zip this session. Files: AppDataModel.swift, AppDataModel+Orbit.swift, CaptureFolderManager.swift, FeedbackMessages.swift, OnboardingStateMachine.swift, UntilProcessingCompleteFilter.swift, Views/{CapturePrimaryView, CaptureOverlayView, TopOverlayButtons, BottomOverlayButtons, ReconstructionPrimaryView, ModelView (QLPreviewController for USDZ), OnboardingView, OnboardingButtonView, PointCloud review...}. Project sets INFOPLIST_KEY_NSCameraUsageDescription, IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 18.0, TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 1,2. Sample deletes Checkpoint/ after the model is produced and deletes the whole capture folder on cancel. Session is nil-ed (`objectCaptureSession = nil`) before creating PhotogrammetrySession 'to free GPU and memory resources'. WWDC23 used 'Snapshots/' as the checkpoint folder name; the current sample uses 'Checkpoint/'. The old guided-capture-sample URL is dead; sfomuseum/ios-guided-capture on GitHub mirrors the 2023 version.

facts.claim: Reading dimensions from the produced USDZ on iOS: ModelIO loads USDZ (`MDLAsset(url:)`, iOS 9+) and gives an axis-aligned bounding box without traversing the hierarchy; RealityKit `Entity(contentsOf:)` (iOS 18 async) / `Entity.load(contentsOf:)` load USDZ and MeshResource.bounds / BoundingBox.extents give per-mesh bounds. SceneKit `SCNScene(url:options:)` and `boundingBox` also load USDZ but are deprecated as of iOS 26 (still compile).
facts.api:
init(url URL: URL)                                       // MDLAsset, iOS 9+
var boundingBox: MDLAxisAlignedBoundingBox { get }      // MDLAsset
func boundingBox(atTime time: TimeInterval) -> MDLAxisAlignedBoundingBox
func childObjects(of objectClass: AnyClass) -> [MDLObject]  // e.g. MDLMesh.self
class func canExportFileExtension(_ extension: String) -> Bool
func export(to URL: URL) throws
@MainActor @preconcurrency convenience init(contentsOf url: URL, withName resourceName: String? = nil) async throws   // Entity, iOS 18+
@MainActor @preconcurrency static func load(contentsOf url: URL, withName resourceName: String? = nil) throws -> Entity  // iOS 13+, blocks main actor
@MainActor @preconcurrency var bounds: BoundingBox { get }   // MeshResource
var extents: SIMD3<Float> { get }                        // BoundingBox
convenience init(url: URL, options: [SCNSceneSource.LoadingOption : Any]? = nil) throws   // SCNScene, iOS 8-26 (deprecated 26)
var boundingBox: (min: SCNVector3, max: SCNVector3) { get set }   // SCNBoundingVolume, deprecated iOS 26
facts.availability: ModelIO iOS 9+; Entity(contentsOf:) iOS 18+; SceneKit APIs deprecated in iOS 26 SDK
facts.notes: MDLAsset.canImportFileExtension lists .usdz/.usd/.usda/.usdc/.obj/.ply/.stl. Volume is not provided by any framework: compute it from MDLMesh vertex + submesh index buffers (signed tetrahedron sum). Entity.visualBounds(relativeTo:) exists (iOS 13) but its doc page was not resolvable in the JSON API this session, so its exact signature is 'likely' only: `func visualBounds(relativeTo referenceEntity: Entity?) -> BoundingBox`. Because ObjectCaptureSession images carry depth, the USDZ is in metres, so bounding box extents are real-world dimensions.

facts.claim: Object size and scene limits: object detection needs objects larger than about 3 in (8 cm) per dimension (sample guidance string); no hard upper size, but WWDC24 says 'Areas larger than 6 feet may have reduced mesh and texture quality unless processed at a higher detail level on Mac'; practical ceiling is the image limit. Avoid reflective, transparent, thin, deformable, and textureless objects; put textureless objects on a textured background.
facts.notes: Sample string: "Can't find your object. It should be larger than 3 in (8 cm) in each dimension." startDetecting() also needs a detected horizontal plane under the screen-centre ray. Flip guidance from WWDC23: flip rigid textured objects (3 orientations), do not flip deformable or symmetric/repetitive-texture objects; unflippable objects get 3 orbits at different heights.

facts.claim: Processing time and resources on iPhone are not quantified by Apple beyond 'In just a few minutes, a USDZ model will be ready' and ProgressInfo.estimatedRemainingTime; an independent benchmark on an iPhone 13 Pro Max found on-device reconstruction within ~4% of an M1 Mac mini (8 GB) and sometimes faster for single objects. Storage need is only exposed via insufficientStorage(requiredBytes:) errors; no fixed '16 GB free' rule exists in docs.
facts.api: case insufficientStorage(requiredBytes: Int64)   // both ObjectCaptureSession.Error and PhotogrammetrySession.Error
facts.notes: Community reports of EXC_BAD_ACCESS in com.apple.corephotogrammetry during reconstruction were iOS 17 beta bugs fixed in beta 6 (Apple staff reply, forum 735017); a later iPhone 15 Pro Max crash report (forum 739417) had no resolution. Mitigations: release the ObjectCaptureSession before reconstruction, keep the app foregrounded, disable idle timer, delete Checkpoint/ after success. Each HEIC at 3024x4032 with depth is roughly 2-4 MB, so a 300-1000 image capture is on the order of 1-4 GB before checkpoints and model.

facts.claim: Device support for Object Capture on iOS is 'iPhone 12 Pro, iPad Pro 2021 and later' (WWDC23/24 wording) i.e. LiDAR plus A14 or newer; the Apple sample README says LiDAR + A14 Bionic or later. iPhone 13 Pro Max (A15, LiDAR) is supported; the Simulator is not.
facts.api:
@MainActor static var isSupported: Bool { get }   // ObjectCaptureSession
static var isSupported: Bool { get }              // PhotogrammetrySession
facts.notes: Forum 734086: an iPad Pro 11 2nd gen (A12Z with LiDAR) fails isSupported, confirming the A14 floor. Both isSupported checks should gate the feature.

facts.claim: No deprecations of any ObjectCaptureSession, ObjectCaptureView, ObjectCapturePointCloudView, PhotogrammetrySession, PhotogrammetrySample or Request/Output members were present in the iOS 26 SDK doc JSON (deprecatedAt is null everywhere checked). Only the SceneKit loading/bounds APIs consulted are marked deprecated at 26.0.
facts.notes: Safe to set deployment target iOS 18.0: everything needed is iOS 17 or 18; iOS 18-only members used are isAutoCaptureEnabled, hideObjectReticle, showShotLocations, ignoreBoundingBox, PhotogrammetrySample(contentsOf:), PhotogrammetrySample.boundingBox, Entity(contentsOf:).

gotchas: Only Detail.reduced compiles on iOS; writing `.modelFile(url: u, detail: .medium)` in an iOS target is an availability error, so keep the default argument (`.modelFile(url: u)`).

ObjectCaptureSession.start() must be called exactly once per instance and both imagesDirectory and checkpointDirectory must be empty (or absent) or the session goes to .failed(directoryNotEmpty). Create a fresh timestamped capture folder per scan.

finish() is silently ignored unless state == .capturing; startDetecting() returns false (no state change) if not in .ready or no horizontal plane under the reticle. Surface the false to the user (sample sets hasDetectionFailed).

The session pauses automatically when the ObjectCaptureView leaves the hierarchy, but NOT when it is merely covered by a sheet/blur; call pause()/resume() manually in that case or you keep taking shots of a covered screen.

PhotogrammetrySession.outputs never ends; wrap it (Apple's UntilProcessingCompleteFilter) or your Task leaks. Always add @unknown default to both Output and Request switches, Apple adds cases (stitchingIncomplete, requestProgressInfo were added in iOS 17.x/18).
cancel() on PhotogrammetrySession is async; wait for .processingCancelled and isProcessing == false before creating another session, otherwise process() throws.
Nil out the ObjectCaptureSession before starting PhotogrammetrySession (sample does this 'to free GPU and memory resources'); running both was the pattern behind reported EXC_BAD_ACCESS crashes.

For OBJ output pass a directory URL built with `appendingPathComponent("Models/", isDirectory: true)`; a plain path without .usdz produces 'Output URL must be specify a .usdz extension file!' and an empty folder. OBJ on iOS is community-confirmed only; plan a ModelIO export fallback.

ObjectCaptureSession.maximumNumberOfInputImages is device-specific and undocumented; read it at runtime and log it on the iPhone 13 Pro Max before designing around a number (community says 1000 on iOS).

Area/scene mode is not an API flag: it is 'skip startDetecting(), call startCapturing() from .ready, add .hideObjectReticle(true), and set PhotogrammetrySession.Configuration.isObjectMaskingEnabled = false'. beginNewScanPass/AfterFlip are invalid in that mode.
isObjectMaskingEnabled defaults to true: for room/scene captures you must set it false (and ignoreBoundingBox = true on iOS 18) or the background is masked away.

The reticle, bounding-box handles, capture dial and coaching overlay are Apple-drawn and cannot be restyled; you can only overlay SwiftUI in a ZStack or via cameraFeedOverlay. When cameraTracking != .normal the ARKit coaching overlay appears; hide your own overlay then.
Model output is metric (depth in the HEICs), so MDLAsset(url:).boundingBox extents are real dimensions; volume must be computed yourself from MDLMesh buffers.
SceneKit SCNScene(url:) and SCNBoundingVolume.boundingBox are deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK (still compile). Prefer ModelIO or RealityKit Entity(contentsOf:) (iOS 18) for USDZ inspection.
Free-Apple-ID sideload is fine: Object Capture needs no entitlements, only NSCameraUsageDescription. Keep UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true during capture and reconstruction.

Delete the Checkpoint/ folder after a successful model (it is large) and the whole capture folder on cancel, as the Apple sample does; otherwise Documents fills quickly (each HEIC is 3024x4032 with depth).
recommendations: Deployment target iOS 18.0 is correct: all Object Capture APIs needed are iOS 17/18 with no deprecations in the iOS 26 SDK, and iOS 18-only helpers (isAutoCaptureEnabled, hideObjectReticle, showShotLocations, ignoreBoundingBox, PhotogrammetrySample(contentsOf:)) are useful for Mapper.

Copy the Apple sample's architecture almost verbatim for the object pipeline: @MainActor @Observable AppDataModel owning ObjectCaptureSession?, PhotogrammetrySession?, CaptureFolderManager (Documents/<ISO8601>/Images, Checkpoint, Models); stateUpdates/feedbackUpdates observed via Tasks; UntilProcessingCompleteFilter for outputs; QLPreviewController for viewing the USDZ. This is the only code path Apple guarantees compiles on an iOS 18 SDK.

Request only `.modelFile(url: models/model-mobile.usdz)` on device (default .reduced). If the product needs OBJ, first try `.modelFile(url: modelsDir /* isDirectory: true */)` and verify on device; keep MDLAsset.export(to: .obj) as fallback for geometry-only OBJ.

For measurements: load the USDZ with `MDLAsset(url:)`, read `boundingBox` for W/H/D (metres, because ObjectCaptureSession stores depth), and iterate `childObjects(of: MDLMesh.self)` vertex/index buffers to compute volume and surface area yourself. Optionally also submit `.bounds` in the same process() call and log whether iOS honours it.

Log `ObjectCaptureSession.maximumNumberOfInputImages` and `PhotogrammetrySession.limits.maximumNumberOfInputImages / maximumInputImageDimension` on first run on the iPhone 13 Pro Max; design the shot budget UI from those values, and enable isOverCaptureEnabled only if you plan a Mac export path.

Use Object Capture's area mode (startCapturing from .ready + hideObjectReticle + isObjectMaskingEnabled=false + ignoreBoundingBox=true) only for small textured scenes (<6 ft per WWDC24); keep RoomPlan/ARKit mesh as the primary room-scale path.
Wrap every switch over CaptureState, Feedback, Output and Request with `@unknown default`, and treat `.failed(ObjectCaptureSession.Error.cancelled)` as a normal restart.
open_questions: Exact value of ObjectCaptureSession.maximumNumberOfInputImages and PhotogrammetrySession.limits on iPhone 13 Pro Max / iOS 18.3.2 (community says 1000 images on iOS; needs a runtime log).

Whether PhotogrammetrySession on iOS actually honours the .bounds, .poses, .pointCloud and .modelEntity requests (docs list them as iOS 17+, Apple's iOS sample marks them 'Not supported yet' without requesting them).
Whether OBJ output (directory URL) works on iOS 18 specifically; only forum users report success, no Apple confirmation.
Typical on-device reconstruction time for a 3-pass scan (~200-300 images) on the A15; only qualitative data ('a few minutes', roughly M1-class) exists.
Exact declaration/doc availability of Entity.visualBounds(relativeTo:) in the iOS 26 SDK JSON (page not resolvable this session); ModelIO boundingBox is the verified alternative.
Minimum free storage that triggers insufficientStorage(requiredBytes:) at session start; not documented, log requiredBytes when it happens.

verdicts.reasoning: Fetched Apple's doc JSON this session for ObjectCaptureSession, ObjectCaptureSession/isSupported and ObjectCaptureSession/init(). All three confirm the claim: metadata.platforms lists only iOS 17.0 and iPadOS 17.0 (no macOS, not deprecated, not beta). Declaration is exactly `@MainActor class ObjectCaptureSession`; `@MainActor static var isSupported: Bool { get }`; `@MainActor init()`. Conforms To lists Identifiable, Observable, Sendable (plus Copyable, Escapable, SendableMetatype, which the claim omitted but did not contradict). The isSupported discussion text matches verbatim: 'If false, attempting to create an ObjectCaptureSession will result in a runtime error.' Topic sections confirm the state machine (CaptureState, start(imagesDirectory:configuration:), startDetecting(), startCapturing(), finish(), cancel(), beginNewScanPass(), beginNewScanPassAfterFlip()) with no reconstruction members, consistent with reconstruction living in PhotogrammetrySession. One nuance, not a refutation: the declaration token block tags platforms as iOS, iPadOS and Mac Catalyst, so a Catalyst build would compile the symbol, but native macOS is absent, so 'NOT macOS' stands. Nothing found that would change the architecture; claim is verified.
verdicts.claim: ObjectCaptureSession exists on iOS 17.0+ (iPadOS 17.0+), NOT macOS. It is a @MainActor class, conforms to Identifiable, Observable, Sendable. Session state machine drives image capture; reconstruction is a separate PhotogrammetrySession phase.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified this session against Apple's doc JSON (fetched raw with curl): metadata.platforms for ObjectCaptureSession = iOS 17.0, iPadOS 17.0 only (no macOS, no visionOS); declaration `@MainActor class ObjectCaptureSession`; Conforms To: Copyable, Escapable, Identifiable, Observable, Sendable, SendableMetatype. Members confirmed: `@MainActor init()` (iOS 17.0), `@MainActor static var isSupported: Bool { get }` (iOS 17.0) with the exact doc text "If false, attempting to create an ObjectCaptureSession will result in a runtime error", `@MainActor var state: ObjectCaptureSession.CaptureState { get }`, CaptureState cases initializing/ready/detecting/capturing/finishing/completed/failed(_:), methods start(imagesDirectory:configuration:), startDetecting(), startCapturing(), beginNewScanPass(), beginNewScanPassAfterFlip(), finish(), cancel(), pause(), resume(), requestImageCapture(). Nothing deprecated on the iOS 26 SDK. PhotogrammetrySession is separately declared (class PhotogrammetrySession, iOS 17.0 / macOS 12.0), confirming the two-phase capture/reconstruction split. Reality lens: Apple forum thread 731148 (Apple engineer): supported devices are iPhone 12 Pro (LiDAR) and newer plus LiDAR iPad Pro 3rd gen+, back cameras + LiDAR only, "simulator is not supported", check isSupported first. Apple sample "Scanning objects using Object Capture" (JSON page) lists requirements: LiDAR, A14 or later, "does not compile for Simulator". GitHub shows 76 Swift files calling ObjectCaptureSession.isSupported in compiling projects (alfianlosari/USDZScanner, sfomuseum/ios-guided-capture, tristanheilman/react-native-object-capture tested on iPhone 16 Pro Max iOS 26); no crash/unavailable reports found for the iPhone 13 Pro class. Two nuances, neither refuting: (1) declaration tokens also list "Mac Catalyst" for the class, isSupported, init, state, CaptureState and ObjectCaptureView, so the symbol compiles in Catalyst builds, but the metadata platforms list only iOS/iPadOS and no native macOS availability exists (claim's "NOT macOS" holds). (2) The current WWDC24 revision of Apple's sample project declares iOS/iPadOS 18.0 as its minimum (sample uses iOS 18 additions), while the API itself is iOS 17.0; iOS 18.3.2 on the target device satisfies both. Evidence on iOS 18-specific runtime behavior is thin (no negative reports found; WebSearch budget was exhausted, so evidence is from Apple JSON docs, one Apple forum thread, and GitHub code search).
verdicts.claim: ObjectCaptureSession exists on iOS 17.0+ (iPadOS 17.0+), NOT macOS. It is a @MainActor class, conforms to Identifiable, Observable, Sendable. Session state machine drives image capture; reconstruction is a separate PhotogrammetrySession phase.
